title: Read saved data and recover from errors
outcome: Recover a valid saved basket without trusting damaged data.
story: Amina wants a basket to survive closing an app. Saved information is text, and that text can be missing, damaged, or an older shape. The app needs a safe recovery rule.

frames.explanation: JSON parsing turns text into structured values.
An error handler recovers to a known safe starting point.

sections.title: Structured values and stored text
paragraphs: An object or array is useful while a program is running. Storage and network messages often carry text. JSON is a text format for representing values such as numbers, strings, arrays, and objects.

JSON.stringify changes a JavaScript value into JSON text. JSON.parse changes JSON text back into a value. Parsing does not prove that the value has the right shape for your application. A perfectly valid JSON number is still the wrong shape for a basket.

sections.title: Expect a saved record to be missing
paragraphs: A new user may have no saved basket. An application should choose a default, such as an empty array. The same is true after a user intentionally clears their data.

A variable in memory lasts only while that program is running. Durable storage, such as a file or database, keeps data for later. Browser storage is tied to an origin and browser profile. It is useful for a small personal draft, but it does not provide shared accounts or backend permissions.

sections.title: Catch the failure you expect
paragraphs: A try block contains an operation that may fail. A catch block handles the resulting error. If JSON.parse sees damaged text, it throws an error rather than guessing what you meant.

Recovering to an empty basket is an explicit policy for this practice app. A real product might preserve the damaged text and offer recovery before replacing it. Avoid silently deleting valuable customer records just to make an error disappear.

sections.title: Check every record after parsing
paragraphs: Our basket must be an array. Every item must have a non-empty name and a positive whole-number quantity. We accept the basket only when all items follow the rules. We return only the fields the application uses.

The browser exercise practises this recovery function with supplied saved text. The independent project connects it to storage and tests a reload. Keep the two checks distinct: reading valid data and proving that the app actually saves it.

words.meaning: A text format used to store and transfer structured values.
Keeping data so it can be loaded later.
Responding deliberately when an operation fails.

explanation: saved is text, including the JSON brackets and field names.
JSON.parse creates the array of records.
The try/catch gives a deliberate alternative if parsing fails. Shape validation still needs to be added.

exercise.title: A safe basket loader
exercise.brief: Write loadBasket(saved). Return a cleaned array of { name, quantity } records. Return [] for missing, damaged, or unacceptable input.

steps.title: Read JSON safely
steps.task: Parse saved text inside try/catch. Missing text and damaged JSON should give an empty array.
steps.hint: Start with if (!saved) return []. Catch parsing errors and return [].

steps.title: Validate the basket shape
steps.task: Require an array of valid records. Reject the entire saved basket if an item has a bad name or quantity.
steps.hint: Use Array.isArray and every. Check that an item exists before reading its properties.

steps.title: Return clean records
steps.task: Trim each name and keep only name and quantity. Ignore unexpected fields instead of copying them into the app.
steps.hint: After validation, map each item to a new { name: item.name.trim(), quantity: item.quantity } object.

cases.label: A valid basket
cases.why: Ordinary saved data must survive loading.

cases.label: No saved draft
cases.why: A first visit needs a useful default.

cases.label: Damaged JSON
cases.why: A parsing error must not crash the recovery function.

cases.label: A JSON object instead of a basket
cases.why: Valid JSON can still have the wrong application shape.

cases.label: An impossible quantity
cases.why: A stored record must satisfy the same rules as a new record.

cases.label: A null record
cases.why: Check the item before accessing its fields.

cases.label: Whitespace and an unexpected field
cases.why: Only recognised application fields should enter the cleaned state.

project.title: A recoverable basket draft
project.brief: Save a fictional basket as JSON text and load it using your recovery function. Begin with the supplied text cases; connect the function to real storage when you set up the local workspace in lesson 7.
deliverables: A loader with a documented recovery policy.
Saved JSON examples for valid and damaged data.
A later reload check in your local app.

milestones.title: Read a good draft
actions: Load it and compare the records.

milestones.title: Recover deliberately
actions: Document when the loader returns an empty basket.

milestones.title: Check the storage boundary
actions: After local setup, save, reload, and confirm the basket remains.

acceptance: Missing and damaged text have a known result.
A real reload is checked before claiming persistence.

tests.expected: Empty basket with the recovery policy explained.

tests.situation: A valid saved basket after reload

project.extension: Return a status beside the basket, such as missing, recovered, or loaded, so the interface can explain what happened.
reflection: What does parsing prove, and what does validation prove?
Could returning [] hide valuable damaged data?
What evidence would demonstrate real persistence?
